records.quote: If chords of a circle are equal in length, then thay are equidistant from the center.
records.claim: Theorem: If chords of a circle are equal in length, then they are equidistant from the center.

records.quote: Theorem diagram with points C, A, Y, X, D, B, M
records.caption: Circle with centre M; chords AB and CD with perpendiculars MX to AB (X on AB) and MY to CD (Y on CD), right angles marked at X and Y; dashed segments MA and MC drawn. Points C, A, Y, X, D, B, M labelled.

records.quote: Given: AB = CD, MX ⊥ AB, MY ⊥ CD
records.text: Given: $AB = CD$, $\overline{MX} \perp \overline{AB}$, $\overline{MY} \perp \overline{CD}$. R.T.P.: Prove that $MX = MY$. Construction: Draw $\overline{MA}$, $\overline{MC}$.

records.quote: Proof: ∵ MX ⊥ AB ∴ AX = 1/2 AB
records.text: Proof: ∵ $\overline{MX}\perp\overline{AB}$ ∴ $AX=\frac{1}{2}AB$. ∵ $\overline{MY}\perp\overline{CD}$ ∴ $CY=\frac{1}{2}CD$. ∵ $AB=CD$ ∴ $AX=CY$. ∵ the two triangles AXM and CYM both have: $AM=CM$; $m(\angle AXM)=m(\angle CYM)=90^\circ$; $AX=CY$ (Proof). ∴ $\triangle AXM \equiv \triangle CYM$. We get: $MX=MY$ (Q.E.D.)
records.notes: Proof printed as a theorem proof, recorded as one block.

records.quote: In congruent circles, chords which are equal in length, are equidistant from the centers
records.claim: Corollary: In congruent circles, chords which are equal in length are equidistant from the centers.

records.label: Example
records.quote: are two equal chords in length in circle M and X is
records.stem: $\overline{AB}$ and $\overline{AC}$ are two equal chords in length in circle M and X is the midpoint of $\overline{AB}$, $\overrightarrow{MX}$ intersects the circle at D, $\overrightarrow{MY} \perp \overline{AC}$ intersects it at Y and intersects the circle at E. Prove that: First: $XD = YE$. Second: $m(\angle YXB) = m(\angle XYC)$.
solution: Given: $AB = AC$, X is the midpoint of $\overline{AB}$, $\overrightarrow{MY} \perp \overline{AC}$
R.T.P.: First: $XD = YE$; Second: $m(\angle YXB) = m(\angle XYC)$
Proof: since X is the midpoint of $\overline{AB}$, therefore $\overrightarrow{MX} \perp \overline{AB}$
since $MD = ME = r$, therefore $MD - MX = ME - MY$, therefore $XD = YE$ (Q.E.D 1)
in $\triangle MXY$: since $MX = MY$, therefore $m(\angle YXM) = m(\angle XYM)$ (1)
From (1) and (2) we get: $m(\angle YXB) = m(\angle XYC)$ (Q.E.D 2)

records.label: Example
records.quote: Two concentric circles M, AB is a chord in the larger circle
records.stem: Two concentric circles M, $\overline{AB}$ is a chord in the larger circle and intersects the smaller circle at C and D, $\overline{AE}$ is a chord in the larger circle and intersects the smaller circle at Z and L. If $m(\angle ABE) = m(\angle AEB)$, then prove that: $CD = ZL$.
solution: Proof: In $\triangle ABC$: $\because m(\angle ABE) = m(\angle AEB)$ $\therefore AB = AE$.
In the larger circle: $AB = AE$ (proof) $\therefore MX = MY$ (theorem)
records.notes: Proof text mentions triangle ABC as printed (likely triangle ABE); not flagged as misprint with certainty.

objectives.label: Relate a chord's length to its distance from the center
objectives.description: Compare chord lengths and distances from the center of a circle: the closer a chord is to the center, the longer it is, and vice versa; use this to compare and bound values.

objectives.label: Show that equal chords are equidistant from the center
objectives.description: Use the theorem and its corollary (same circle or congruent circles) that equal chords are equidistant from the center, and apply it to find unknown lengths and distances.

objectives.label: Use the converse: equidistant chords are equal
objectives.description: Use the converse that chords equidistant from the center of a circle (or congruent circles) are equal in length, to find lengths, values and angles.

objectives.label: Solve proofs combining chord properties
objectives.description: Prove statements in composite figures (concentric, intersecting circles, inscribed triangles) by combining the theorem, its converse, and chord-midpoint perpendicularity.
